summary: Critical authorization flaws confirmed by reading both local and deployed Firestore rules. No exploit executed, no production writes, no rules deployed. Client fixes do not secure the database.

findings.issue: Authenticated callers can enumerate families and append themselves via request.resource.data.memberUids; ownership fields are mutable.
findings.recommendation: Private family reads, non-enumerable invitation capability lookup, validated atomic joins, immutable creator and protected membership changes.

findings.issue: Recursive family write permission grants every member access to membership roles and all shared writes, bypassing client view-only permissions.
findings.recommendation: Non-overlapping membership rules and explicit role enforcement on shared content using existing trusted membership.

findings.issue: Client household notifications and member removal/deletion write other users' private documents and are denied.
findings.recommendation: Shared household events with per-user read receipts and an explicit validated membership/unlink protocol; preserve private user ownership.

findings.check: Update Bypass / Type Safety / Resource Exhaustion
findings.issue: No field allowlists, schema validation, or size limits for document creates and updates.
findings.recommendation: Validate each supported document schema on both create and update after defining compatibility for existing data.
